notes: Identity verified from title page: Can lies be detected unconsciously?, Wen Ying Moi and David R. Shanks, ORIGINAL RESEARCH, published 25 August 2015, doi: 10.3389/fpsyg.2015.01221; supplied text contains the full ten-page primary article, including both experiments, results and references. No PDF was supplied. Only replication n_r and es_value_r are assigned; other fields are unassigned placeholders. Target conflict: study_r explicitly specifies Experiment 1, whose thinking-mode effect on discrimination is on printed p. 4; locators_r specifies p. 7, which reports Experiment 2. The neutral description applies to both. No target selected by row order or numeric matching. Experiment 1 candidate: discrimination d-prime, 3 (thinking mode) × 2 (gender) between-subjects ANOVA; printed partial eta squared η2p = 0.008, F(2,110) = 0.43, same-test p = 0.649 (exact). Final assigned participant groups on p. 3: UT 37, CT 40, ID 39; candidate analytic N arithmetic 37 + 40 + 39 = 116. Participants are the analytic units; video actors and videos are stimuli, and recruitment-source counts must not be added again. The source states participants were included and randomly assigned; no further exclusions are described in Experiment 1 Method/Results. Experiment 2 alternative at supplied page locator: discrimination d-prime, same factorial ANOVA, printed partial eta squared η2p = 0.002, F(2,104) = 0.12, same-test p = 0.887 (exact). Groups on p. 6: UT 37, CT 40, ID 33; candidate N arithmetic 37 + 40 + 33 = 110. Participants, not actors or videos, are analytic units; no further exclusions are described there. Both N sums remain candidates because experiment correspondence is unresolved. Partial eta squared is explicitly printed (η2p); no conversion to ordinary eta squared or other metric performed. Both candidate p values are retained only in notes because p_r is unassigned.
